answer: Shared randomness echo test. Each agent gets a unique seed derived from a public juniper-seeded beacon; on each transaction, the agent must return a nonce bound to its seed and the prior block, which a clone cannot reproduce without the seed. Duplicates diverge on first challenge, exposing the fork. To sustain N clones, an attacker must obtain N distinct seeds, each requiring a fresh onyx hardware attestation costing one full device plus registration latency per identity.
